bar_name: WS225 provider-neutral candidate admission bar (pre-qualification admission; NOT Provider Selection)
burden_policy: Burden estimates use coarse bands (HOURS / DAYS / WEEKS / UNKNOWN) and are stated only where a sealed probe bounds them. No pseudo-precision: point estimates are forbidden.

RUNTIME_VERIFIED_required_before: S3 SUPPORTED counts are census-grade (DIRECTLY_VERIFIED probe + test inventory), never mere construction claims
S4 bounded replay proof (minimum one tape + clean-process replay)

fairness_rule: The same stage rules, the same frozen denominator (29 cards, 17 micro areas, 135 fixtures), the same evidence vocabulary, and the same failure semantics apply to every candidate including XMage and Forge. Different outcomes from different evidence are fairness; different standards for the same evidence would be incumbency bias (tested in INCUMBENCY_BIAS_TEST.json).
funnel: S1 architecture / Rules authority / legal-action / hidden-info feasibility
S3 frozen-card and micro-rules denominator screen
funnel_rule: Cheap terminal blockers stop expensive downstream work. No candidate reaches S5 spend while a terminal blocker stands at S0-S4.
incumbency_rule: XMage and Forge must pass the same stages with the same evidence grades. Lane-specific harnesses (XMage full-game lane, Forge protocol2 bridge) are mapping layers, never alternative standards. Historical effort already spent is not evidence.
semantic_capabilities_required: adapter feasibility (named mapping layer, no twin-shaped mandate)
Rules Core sole authority (sole legality + rules-randomness authority)
authoritative legal-action surface (complete options, no reconstruction)
actual-card denominator (29/29 SUPPORTED with dedicated tests inventoried)
semantic replay feasibility (bounded proof, then campaign)
process isolation (one game per clean process; no shared mutable state)
licensing/integration topology (declared model, satisfied at selection)
